title: SILO: Semantic Integration for Location Prediction with Large Language Models

problem.claim: Next location prediction is a human mobility modeling task with applications in personalized recommendation, urban planning, and location-based services.

gap.claim: Prompt-based LLM approaches face a gap between textual semantic context and human mobility transition patterns.

contributions.claim: SILO constructs a hybrid semantic space integrating ID-based embeddings, text-derived semantics, and auxiliary contextual information for sequential mobility modeling.
SILO uses user-centric prompts with user context embedded in a special token and processes them with hybrid ID-context location-sequence embeddings through an LLM prediction backbone.
SILO introduces a dual-logits strategy that combines sequential transition logits with user-profile-guided semantic preference logits.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on two large-scale real-world mobility datasets reportedly show that SILO significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that the experiments validate SILO's effectiveness in modeling complex mobility patterns through semantic integration using LLMs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Next location prediction is important in human mobility modeling and has multiple practical applications.
Prior work uses prompt-based LLMs and pretrained knowledge for next location prediction.
Existing approaches struggle to connect textual semantic understanding with mobility transition patterns.
SILO integrates hybrid semantic representations, user-centric prompts, LLM processing, and a dual-logits prediction strategy.
The authors report superior performance over state-of-the-art baselines on two real-world mobility datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines ID-based embeddings, text-derived semantics, auxiliary context, user-centric prompts, and two types of logits.

interpretation.claim: Combining structured transition information with semantic and user-context signals may help address mismatches between language representations and mobility patterns.

application.claim: Other sequential prediction systems could consider integrating domain-specific identifiers, semantic context, user context, and complementary prediction signals.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which component or combination is responsible for the reported performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two datasets.
The abstract does not provide evaluation metrics, quantitative gains, baseline names, or statistical details.
The abstract does not specify the auxiliary contextual information, LLM model, training procedure, or ablation results.
